body.html: Who Somerset Rama 9 is right for — opened in 2020, Somerset Rama 9 Bangkok is one of the newest and highest-rated serviced apartments in the Rama 9 corridor, scoring 9.1 from 3,480 reviews on Trip.com, 8.7 on Booking.com, and ranking #7 of over 1,380 Bangkok hotels on TripAdvisor (4.9/5 from 1,204 reviews) · what sets it apart from ordinary hotels in the area is that it is a genuine serviced apartment — meaning every unit has a real kitchen, a washing machine-dryer (Executive and Premier tiers), a living area and a dining space, not just a hotel bed · the guests who rave about it most consistently are families on multi-night stays, business travelers working from the apartment, and relatives caring for patients at Bangkok Hospital (BDMS), which sits roughly 2–2.5 km away — about 8 minutes by Grab · the things real reviewers mention most are spotlessly clean rooms, staff service that goes well beyond expectations, and the relief of having a kitchen when you need to eat simply and cheaply across many days · it has also been named Thailand's Leading Hotel Residences 2025 at the World Travel Awards and earned TripAdvisor's Best of the Best 2023, reflecting a track record of consistent quality

Location and getting around — the detail that makes long-stay guests happiest — Somerset Rama 9 sits at 22 Ratchadaphisek Road, Huai Khwang, Bangkok 10310 · MRT Phra Ram 9 (Blue Line) is roughly 450 m away — about a 5-minute flat walk · from Phra Ram 9 you can connect to the whole city; it takes around 15–20 minutes to reach the Sukhumvit corridor and then transfer to the BTS at Asok · the hotel is also just a 3-minute walk from Central Plaza Grand Rama 9, which means a supermarket, Lotus, pharmacies, dozens of restaurants and a 7-Eleven are all within easy reach — a genuine advantage when you're cooking in-room across a week-long stay · for anyone traveling for medical reasons, Bangkok Hospital (BDMS) headquarters on Soi Soonvijai 7, New Petchburi Road, is approximately 2–2.5 km away — roughly 8 minutes by Grab · this is close enough to drop off a patient, return to the hotel to rest or work, and head back quickly when needed · the hotel can also arrange advance-booked shuttle transfers; just ask at Front Desk · free parking is available for those arriving by car

"Brought my mother to Bangkok Hospital for treatment — Grab there took under 10 minutes. Having the kitchen meant I could make her congee in the room. The rooftop pool was beautiful and the staff helped with everything without any fuss — the best long-stay choice we've found near the hospital."

Room types — what you actually get in each category — the 445 units span 36 floors and cover several distinct types · the entry-level Studio Executive comes with a Queen bed or two Singles, a full kitchen with sink, induction hob, microwave, fridge and basic cookware, plus a work desk and flat-screen TV · the Deluxe King Room adds a King-size bed and often a higher-floor city view · the Premier One Bedroom separates the bedroom from a proper living room, adds a washer-dryer in-unit, and makes week-long stays noticeably more comfortable · and at the top sits the Two-Bedroom Executive at 90 sqm, located on floors 24–35, which suits families or groups traveling together and needing genuinely separate sleeping spaces · one thing reviewers mention repeatedly about the room finish is how genuinely new and clean everything feels: "spotlessly clean, completely odorless bedding," "the housekeeping team leaves little origami animals on the towels every day" · Wi-Fi is free throughout and the in-room wired connection is available for remote workers — only a handful of reviews mention occasional TV-streaming buffering on some units

Pool, gym and amenities — well above what the price suggests — the outdoor pool on the 8th floor is open every day from 06:00 to 22:00, with a separate kids' pool alongside · there is also an indoor pool for overcast or cool-season mornings · the city-view gym on a high floor is the amenity guests mention most enthusiastically — with full cardio and weights equipment against a panoramic Bangkok skyline, multiple reviews call it "100-point gym access included for free" · rounding out the leisure deck are a sauna, steam room, yoga classes, a kids' club and a massage spa · for families staying to manage medical treatment, the combination of a kids' club (so younger children have something to do), a proper kitchen (so meals stay manageable) and a pool (so recovery days don't feel cooped up) is a combination that's surprisingly hard to find this close to the hospital district · free parking on site; the hotel can arrange airport or hospital shuttle transfers with advance notice

Service — the consistent reason guests come back — the single most talked-about element across Trip.com (9.2/10 for service), Booking.com (9.3/10 for staff) and TripAdvisor is the quality of the team · reviewers name individual staff members by name and describe moments like a complimentary birthday cake prepared in secret, help tracking down a misplaced luggage item, and unprompted room upgrades when the hotel has availability · for guests managing a medical stay, this attentiveness is especially valuable: several reviews describe staff going out of their way to arrange early morning hospital runs, recommend pharmacies nearby, and calmly assist guests arriving stressed after a long flight · the tone in reviews is less "hotel service" and more "someone genuinely looking after you," which aligns with what a serviced residence is supposed to feel like

"Breakfast was adequate — not a huge variety and not cheap — but with a proper kitchen in the room we mostly cooked for ourselves anyway. What kept us here was the gym view and the staff: every single person we interacted with was kind and genuinely helpful."

Real guest feedback — the full picture, positives and negatives — pulling from Trip.com (3,480 reviews, 9.1), Booking.com (870+ reviews, 8.7), and TripAdvisor (#7 Bangkok, 4.9/5 from 1,204) the picture is consistently positive but not without honest caveats · what guests praise: immaculately clean rooms that feel brand-new, exceptional staff service with personal touches, a 5-minute MRT walk and Central Rama 9 right next door, a full working kitchen and in-room washing machine that make multi-week stays viable, and a city-view gym that reviews call one of Bangkok's best included facilities · what guests criticize: the breakfast buffet offers limited variety at a high price (~THB 350/person) and is consistently described as the weakest part of the package — most guests skip it and cook in-room or eat at Central Rama 9 · some reviews mention the outdoor pool is quite cold, especially November through January and in early mornings · a minority of reviews describe long Check-in queues — up to 2 hours on busy holiday weekends · and a handful of rooms report occasional Wi-Fi TV buffering · none of these is a dealbreaker, and the overwhelming majority of reviewers say they would return

Prices and value — especially compelling for long stays and medical visits — rooms start from around THB 2,900–3,200/night for a Studio Executive in a normal period, rising to roughly THB 3,800–5,500 for a Premier One Bedroom and THB 6,800 and up for a Two-Bedroom Executive · compared with an ordinary hotel of the same star tier nearby, Somerset's nightly rate may look slightly higher on night one — but over three nights or more, cooking your own meals in the kitchen, washing clothes in-room and having a proper living space instead of a single bed will materially reduce total trip spend · for families managing a hospital stay — where meals, laundry and a calm place to return to each day matter enormously — the math is even more favorable · breakfast is not included in the room rate by default; it is available at around THB 350/person/day, but the consistent advice in reviews is to use the kitchen and the mall instead

Bottom line and booking tips — Somerset Rama 9 Bangkok is the best long-stay serviced apartment option in the Rama 9 area for families, business travelers and anyone visiting Bangkok Hospital · brand-new rooms, full kitchen, in-room laundry, a top-10 Bangkok service reputation and a 5-minute MRT walk all combine into a property that actually feels like living rather than just sleeping · Practical tips before you book: request a high-floor room (20th floor or above) facing the G Tower or city side if noise matters to you — some reviews mention night-market sound on lower floors facing the road · if you arrive on a peak holiday weekend, be prepared for a wait at Check-in; drop bags with the front desk and head to Central Rama 9 while your room is readied · skip the breakfast package and budget that THB 350/person toward the Lotus or supermarket in the mall instead · and if your stay involves daily hospital visits, ask Front Desk about advance-scheduled shuttle transfers — it is a significantly less stressful option than hailing a Grab at 7 a.m. every morning

honestSummary: Somerset Rama 9 Bangkok is the best long-stay serviced apartment option in the Rama 9 area for families, business travelers and guests visiting Bangkok Hospital — full kitchen, in-room laundry, top-10-Bangkok service quality and a 5-minute MRT walk, all in a hotel that genuinely feels like living rather than just sleeping · the honest caveats are that breakfast is not a strong point and the outdoor pool can be cold in the cool season.
honestChecks: If you want an all-you-can-eat buffet breakfast included in your rate — the breakfast here costs ~THB 350/person extra and has a limited spread → use the in-room kitchen and the Lotus supermarket in Central Rama 9 (3-minute walk); you'll eat better and spend less

If you're planning to swim outdoors at dawn every day — the pool runs cold in the November–January cool season and early mornings → use the indoor pool on those days, or plan outdoor swims for the sun-warmed afternoon hours

If you're arriving on a peak holiday Friday or Saturday evening — Check-in can have long queues; some reviewers waited up to 2 hours → drop bags at the front desk when you arrive, walk to Central Rama 9 for dinner, and come back when the queue has cleared

tips.title: Getting to Bangkok Hospital
tips.body: Bangkok Hospital (BDMS) headquarters on Soi Soonvijai 7, New Petchburi Road, is about 2–2.5 km away — roughly 8 minutes by Grab. The hotel can book shuttle transfers in advance; ask Front Desk the night before an early appointment.

tips.title: Use the kitchen, skip the buffet
tips.body: The breakfast buffet costs ~THB 350/person with limited variety. Central Rama 9 is a 3-minute walk with a Lotus supermarket and dozens of restaurant options — buy breakfast ingredients and cook in-room to save several hundred baht a day across a long stay.

tips.title: Ask for a high-floor city-side room
tips.body: Rooms on the 20th floor and above facing the G Tower or city direction offer the best views and the least road and market noise. Ask at booking or check-in whether any recently renovated units are available.

tips.title: Beat the check-in queue
tips.body: On busy holiday weekends, check-in queues can reach 2 hours. Drop bags at the front desk when you arrive, walk to Central Rama 9 while your room is prepared, and come back when the crowd has thinned. Online check-in via the app can also speed things up.
